inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow add-back (us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense = $48M; H1 2026 $46M). No separate net-share-settlement withholding tag is published; at 0.55% of revenue the omission is immaterial (<$0.10/share).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 treasury purchases $100M (1.42M shares); 2026 YTD zero -- cash is going to the $3.36/share dividend (~$385M/yr) and debt. Flat count is a modelling convention: SBC is expensed in the flows, and at 0.55% of revenue the count would drift <0.4%/yr unfunded.
inputs.share_count_basis: Q2 2026 weighted-average diluted shares 115.3M (10-Q filed 2026-07-31); cover-page outstanding 114.38M at 2026-06-30 plus ~0.9M dilutive awards. Held FLAT: SBC fully expensed, so diluting the count as well would double-charge. The FY rows of the Metrics CSV (~224M) are shares ISSUED including 109.9M in treasury, not outstanding.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:00:02Z regular close (Yahoo chart API; last regular session before the 2026-09-28 build)
inputs.net_debt_note: Borrowings $5,217M (us-gaap:DebtLongtermAndShorttermCombinedAmount: long-term 4,452 + short-term 765) less cash incl. restricted $691M, both at 2026-06-30. The Metrics CSV TotalDebt column (4,452) is long-term debt only; the DCF uses total borrowings. Operating lease liabilities (~$170M PV, $88M/yr payments) are EXCLUDED because the lease cost already sits inside EBITDA (treatment B). Unfunded pension/OPEB obligations are not deducted -- no reliable XBRL figure was pulled; a ~$400M deficit would be ~$3.5/share and is listed under key risks.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. 10-year UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.2 = cost of equity ~10.2%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0% (FY2025 interest paid $215M on ~$5.0B average borrowings = 4.3%, marginal issuance higher), 4.0% after tax. Market weights: equity $7.7B (115.3M x $66.97) vs net debt $4.5B, D/(D+E) ~37%. WACC = 0.63 x 10.2 + 0.37 x 4.0 = 7.9%, rounded to 8.0%. ONE WACC across all three scenarios: cyclicality and leverage risk are priced in the bear scenario's flows and its 25% weight, not stacked on the discount rate (adaptations section f).
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost, by construction: US GAAP ASC 842 operating lease expense ($90M FY2025, $88M cash payments) is inside cost of sales / SG&A and therefore inside EBITDA and OCF. Lease liabilities are excluded from net debt. No finance leases are tagged. D&A is ex right-of-use amortisation, so cash-tax EBIT is not double-charged.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge: noncontrolling interest of $79M (2026-06-30) deducted from EV. NCI share of earnings is ~$1M/yr, so the flows are effectively attributable already.
inputs.tax_note: Cash taxes paid: FY2021-25 = 122, 78, 158, 111, 159 ($M) -- ~13% of pre-tax income on average, against a GAAP effective rate of 16-19% (FY2024 15.8%, FY2025 16.4%, H1 2026 25.8%). The engine taxes unlevered EBIT, so the interest shield belongs in the WACC, not here: rate starts at 19% (management's normalised ETR guidance range 18-19%) and ramps to 21% by year 3.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, cyclical: industrials'), built via the Drivers route with the cyclical adaptations applied: risk charged once in the flows, single 8% WACC, terminal cap held to 12-15x (not the 20x compounder default) because Chemical Intermediates is a commodity-spread business and the 10-year revenue CAGR is -1%. FY0 = FY2025 (Dec year-end); year 1 is FY2026, nine months of which are done -- H1 2026 revenue $4,690M (+2.5%), Q2 +10% YoY, management guiding Q3 adjusted EPS to approach Q2's $1.97, FY2026 OCF approaching $900M and capex ~$400M. FY2026 OCF guidance sits ~$180M below the component build's implied levered OCF; the gap is the 2026 working-capital rebuild after a depressed Q4 2025 ($1,973M revenue quarter) and is timing, not margin. First-year owner-FCF margin from the components (~9.1% unlevered) compares with a FY2025 reported-FCF margin of 4.8% that carried $96M restructuring and a 6.2% capex year; the FY2024 unlevered equivalent was ~9.5%. Buybacks: real but modest ($100M FY2025, nil 2026 YTD) -- the flat count is mostly convention, see buyback_note. Price is the 2026-09-25 regular close, not an after-hours print.

equity_bridge.note: us-gaap:MinorityInterest at 2026-06-30 (Q2 2026 10-Q); NCI earnings ~$1M/yr so the flows are attributable, deduct the stock once here

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-cycle nominal growth after a FY2026-27 recovery bounce. Neither the equity CAGR (buyback-distorted) nor the FCF CAGRs (cycle-endpoint-dependent) are usable anchors; revenue has compounded at -1%/yr over ten years (FY2015 $9,648M to FY2025 $8,752M) through portfolio pruning and the 2023-25 chemicals downcycle.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3-yr CAGR +4.9% vs revenue -6.1% and EPS -13.6%: the divergence is buyback cadence ($900M in FY2021, ~$1B FY2022, $100M FY2025) plus the FY2022-25 downcycle, not organic compounding. The 5-yr owner-FCF CAGR of -18% runs from a FY2020 cash-generation peak (working-capital release in the COVID trough) to a FY2025 restructuring year; the 3-yr +8.4% runs from a FY2022 working-capital-build trough. Both endpoints are cyclical noise.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF minus SBC, interest income nil): FY2020 1,028; FY2021 994; FY2022 295; FY2023 482; FY2024 625; FY2025 376. SBC is 0.5-0.7% of revenue throughout, so the owner and reported series move together; SBC is not eating the growth here -- the cycle is.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +7%: H1 +2.5% with Q2 +10%, Q3 guided flat-to-Q2 on a $2,202M prior-year quarter and Q4 lapping a depressed $1,973M quarter -- ~$9.37B. FY2027 +4% as CI spread recovery completes, then GDP-like 2.5-3% nominal: specialty volume growth and circular ramp net of Fibers decline (~12% of sales, secular).
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 16.8% = H1 actual 16.2% (GAAP EBIT-before-interest 499 + D&A 263 on 4,690) plus Q2's 17.6% exit rate held through H2. Ramps to 18.0% mid-cycle by FY2029: the 2015-2024 GAAP range was 15.8-19.7%, midpoint ~17.7%, plus ~0.5pp net from the $125-150M cost programme after Fibers mix drag. Does NOT return to the FY2024 19% specialty-peak.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 $400M guided (4.3%) is a post-Kingsport trough; FY2019-2025 averaged 6.3% including the methanolysis build. Mid-cycle 5.3% (~$500M+) vs D&A settling at 5.0% -- modest growth reinvestment, no second methanolysis plant in base.
base.wc_rationale: Manufacturer: receivables + inventory exceed payables by ~13% of revenue (FY2025 balance sheet), so growth consumes 13c per incremental revenue dollar. Negative capture, per the adaptations checklist.
base.terminal_rationale: Cap 14x owner FCF binds (Gordon at 8%/2.5% would be 18.6x). Today's EV/unlevered-owner-FCF is ~14x on the FY2026 build, so the exit multiple assumes no re-rating.

bull.narrative: CI spreads stay expanded through 2027, specialty volumes recover with autos/construction, circular revenue keeps doubling and a second methanolysis site is funded from cash flow (hence capex 5.8%). Margin reaches the FY2024 specialty-peak 20% and holds. Cap 15x still below the 20x compounder default.

bear.narrative: H2 2026 fades (FY +4%), the cycle turns down again in 2027 as CI spreads compress and feedstock costs rise (-4%), and margins revisit FY2025's ~15% before settling at 16% -- below mid-cycle because Fibers keeps shrinking and the cost programme only offsets inflation. Growth 2% thereafter, terminal 2%, cap 12x (the low end of the cyclical range). Leverage at 3.4x ND/EBITDA makes this path uncomfortable but not a solvency event: the dividend is the pressure valve.

scenario_narratives.base: Eastman's value rests on three axes: (1) whether Chemical Intermediates' spread recovery (segment EBIT from a $30M loss to +$58M in Q2 2026) is a cycle turn or a spike; (2) whether specialty volumes in Advanced Materials/AFP recover with autos and construction while Fibers keeps declining; (3) whether the Kingsport methanolysis platform (~$60M incremental earnings, circular revenue doubled in H1 2026) becomes a durable margin contributor. Base: FY2026 revenue ~$9.4B (+7%) at a 16.8% EBITDA margin, ramping to 18% mid-cycle by FY2029 with the $125-150M cost programme netted against Fibers drag; capex normalises from the $400M trough to ~5.3% of revenue; 2.5% terminal growth; terminal capped at 14x owner FCF (roughly today's multiple, no re-rating). Leverage (~$4.5B net debt, 3.4x EBITDA) takes ~40% of enterprise value off the top, which is why equity value is so sensitive to the margin path.
scenario_narratives.bull: The cycle turns properly: CI spreads hold through 2027, auto and building demand recovers, circular products keep doubling and management funds a second methanolysis line from cash flow. Revenue compounds 9%/6%/5% then 3-4%, EBITDA margin reaches the FY2024 specialty-peak 20% and holds, capex runs at 5.8% for the expansion. Terminal cap 15x. Requires three independent things to go right, which is why it gets 25% not 35%.
scenario_narratives.bear: H2 2026 fades, a second downleg arrives in 2027 (revenue -4%, margin back to ~15%) as CI spreads compress and feedstock costs rise; margins settle at 16% because Fibers keeps shrinking and cost savings only match inflation. Terminal 2% growth at a 12x cap. With $5.2B of borrowings the dividend becomes the pressure valve; interest cover (~3.9x) holds, so this is an earnings and multiple path, not a solvency one.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: a commodity-spread segment that swung from loss to profit in one year, 3.4x ND/EBITDA and ~45% of costs in raw materials and energy mean a second downleg is a live path, not a tail. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs CI spreads, specialty end-market recovery and the circular ramp all to hold simultaneously. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF component DCF for a levered, cyclical US specialty-chemicals company. Risk is charged once, in the flows and weights (25% bear), not by inflating the discount rate: one 8% USD WACC across all scenarios. The terminal cap is held to 12-15x rather than the 20x compounder default because the decade of revenue history compounds at -1% and a third of EBITDA is commodity-spread dependent. SBC is fully expensed and the diluted count held flat. Net debt is total borrowings at 2026-06-30 with operating leases left in EBITDA (treatment B) and NCI deducted once in the bridge.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin path: every 1pp of terminal EBITDA margin is roughly $120M of EBITDA and, at 14x on the post-tax flow, ~$9/share -- the single most consequential assumption
Leverage: ~$4.5B net debt against a ~$7.7B market cap means a 10% move in enterprise value is a ~16% move in equity value
Chemical Intermediates spread reversal (the Q2 2026 swing from -$30M to +$58M segment EBIT can run in reverse)
Fibers (12% of sales) is a structurally declining cigarette-filter business; the base assumes it is absorbed by the cost programme, not that it stabilises
Unfunded pension/OPEB obligations are not in the bridge; if the deficit is ~$400M that is ~$3.5/share of downside to every scenario
Methanolysis execution and mass-balance/regulatory scrutiny of recycled-content claims
Terminal cap choice: moving the base cap from 14x to 18x (the Gordon value) would add ~$15/share -- the re-rating thesis is deliberately excluded
